question: When literal and parameterized mechanisms coexist in the same registry with equal confidence, does the literal mechanism's universal matching create false accepts — selecting the literal mechanism and returning an incorrect bound_action URL for unseen resources?
hypothesis: In a shared registry containing both a literal mechanism (parameter_slots=[], fixed URL for resource 1) and a parameterized mechanism (parameter_slots=['id'], template URL with ${id} slot), both at equal confidence (0.95), the kernel's resolve() will select the literal mechanism for unseen resource IDs (2, 3, 4) due to alphabetical iteration order (literal-fetch-posts-1 < param-fetch-posts), producing a bound_action URL pointing to resource 1 instead of the requested resource. This constitutes a false accept: the kernel returns EXECUTABLE with an incorrect URL. When the parameterized mechanism has strictly higher confidence, it will be selected correctly with the correct URL.
falsifier: The hypothesis is FALSIFIED if: (1) In the equal-confidence shared-registry condition, the parameterized mechanism is selected (not the literal) for unseen resource IDs — indicating the kernel has a specificity tiebreaker or iteration order differs from alphabetical; OR (2) The bound_action URL for the equal-confidence condition correctly targets the requested resource (e.g., /posts/2 for id=2) — indicating the literal mechanism's bound_action is somehow resource-aware; OR (3) Both mechanisms have equal confidence but the kernel sorts by something other than confidence first (e.g., parameter_slots count). Any of these would mean the false-accept scenario does not occur as predicted.
baselines: B_LITERAL_ONLY: Only literal mechanism registered (confidence=0.95). Resolve with params={id: 2}. Must return EXECUTABLE with bound_action url ending /posts/1. Verifies the literal mechanism's universal matching behavior in isolation (reproduces prior finding).

B_PARAM_ONLY: Only parameterized mechanism registered (confidence=0.95). Resolve with params={id: 2}. Must return EXECUTABLE with bound_action url ending /posts/2. Verifies the parameterized mechanism's correct behavior in isolation (reproduces prior finding).
B_COLD: No mechanism registered. Resolve with params={id: 2}. Must return UNKNOWN. Verifies kernel abstains (reproduces prior finding).
positive_control: Register only the parameterized mechanism (confidence=0.95). Resolve with params={id: 3}. Must return EXECUTABLE with bound_action url https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/3. Execute HTTP GET, verify status 200 and JSON keys [userId, id, title, body]. This confirms the parameterized pipeline works correctly when no literal mechanism is present to interfere.
null_control: Register only the literal mechanism (confidence=0.95). Resolve with params={id: 4}. Must return EXECUTABLE with bound_action url https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1 (the literal's fixed URL, NOT /posts/4). This confirms the literal mechanism returns a wrong URL for unseen resources — the baseline false-accept behavior that the shared-registry test will amplify.
measurement_validity: Test substrate is jsonplaceholder.typicode.com — same as prior experiment (EXP-GRAPH-33528827169). Deterministic, no auth, no session, no DOM. This is a shared-registry competition test, not a real-web-complexity claim.
Each condition uses a fresh kernel instance with a dedicated registry file containing exactly the specified mechanisms. No cross-condition contamination.

Resolution is measured by: (a) which mechanism_id is selected; (b) the bound_action URL; (c) the resolution status. HTTP execution is performed only for EXECUTABLE resolutions to verify the bound_action produces a valid response.

Registry file ordering is deterministic: MechanismRegistry.replace() writes mechanisms sorted by mechanism_id. This means literal-fetch-posts-1 is written before param-fetch-posts, establishing the iteration order that the kernel's resolve() uses for candidate selection.
No outcome-bearing measurements during DESIGN phase. All measurements deferred to EXECUTE.
Seed无关 — deterministic test, no RNG.

The prior experiment (EXP-GRAPH-33528827169) used isolated registries per condition. This experiment explicitly uses SHARED registries to test competition — the key gap identified by the auditor (V_ISOLATION_NO_COMPETITION).

conditions.description: Shared registry, equal confidence, resolve for unseen resource id=2
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: literal-fetch-posts-1 is selected OR bound_action url ends /posts/1 instead of /posts/2

conditions.description: Shared registry, equal confidence, resolve for unseen resource id=3
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: literal-fetch-posts-1 is selected OR bound_action url ends /posts/1 instead of /posts/3

conditions.description: Shared registry, equal confidence, resolve for unseen resource id=4
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: literal-fetch-posts-1 is selected OR bound_action url ends /posts/1 instead of /posts/4

conditions.description: Shared registry, parameterized has higher confidence (0.99 vs 0.95)
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: literal-fetch-posts-1 is selected OR bound_action url ends /posts/1

conditions.description: Shared registry, literal has higher confidence (0.99 vs 0.95)
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: param-fetch-posts is selected OR bound_action url ends /posts/2

conditions.description: Only literal mechanism, resolve for unseen resource (baseline false accept)
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: UNKNOWN returned OR bound_action url ends /posts/4

conditions.description: Only parameterized mechanism, resolve for unseen resource (baseline correct)
conditions.falsifier_triggered_if: UNKNOWN returned OR bound_action url ends /posts/1 instead of /posts/3

decision_rule: SHARED-REGISTRY-UNSAFE if ANY of the equal-confidence shared-registry conditions (shared-equal-confidence-id2, shared-equal-confidence-id3, shared-equal-confidence-id4) has the literal mechanism selected instead of the parameterized mechanism, OR the bound_action URL targets the wrong resource. SHARED-REGISTRY-SAFE if ALL equal-confidence conditions select the parameterized mechanism with correct URLs. CONFIDENCE-DOMINATES if the parameterized-higher-confidence condition correctly selects parameterized and the literal-higher-confidence condition correctly selects literal. BASELINE-CONSISTENT if literal-only, param-only, and cold conditions match their expected resolutions.
product_consequence_positive: If SHARED-REGISTRY-SAFE: literal universal matching does not create false accepts when parameterized mechanisms are present with equal confidence. The current kernel behavior is safe for shared registries. C-PARAM-INHERIT can advance with the existing literal/parameterized coexistence design. No kernel fix needed for the shared-registry competition issue.
product_consequence_negative: If SHARED-REGISTRY-UNSAFE: literal mechanisms create false accepts in shared registries when confidence is tied. The kernel needs a specificity tiebreaker (prefer more parameter_slots when confidence is equal) or literal mechanisms need a fixed_resource constraint before C-PARAM-INHERIT can be declared validated for production use. The fix must be implemented and re-tested before the claim advances.
estimated_cost: Negligible — 8 resolution calls (no HTTP for cold/wrong-URL conditions, HTTP for correct-URL conditions to verify bound_action validity). Same substrate as prior experiment. Execution time < 30 seconds.
expected_information_gain: HIGH for C-PARAM-INHERIT. This is the exact gap identified by the auditor (V_ISOLATION_NO_COMPETITION) and the parent handoff. The experiment directly answers whether literal universal matching is safe in the realistic shared-registry scenario. Both positive and negative outcomes change the product decision: positive → no fix needed; negative → kernel fix required before claim advancement.
